newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar closes stronger as AUD rallies.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar closes stronger as AUD rallies.

text.p: Encouraged by a sharply stronger Australian currency, the New Zealand dollar rallied on Thursday, breaking resistance at US 69 cents to close on a bullish note.

"It's broken higher along with the Aussie dollar. We've seen a lot of the longer term short guys buying back above a break of 69 the figure. Technically, it's quite a bullish sign," said Tania Pye at Bankers Trust.

The Kiwi closed at US$0.6915/22 and at 68.64 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from 0.6874/81 and 68.47 at its local open. Meanwhile, the Australian dollar rose to multi-year highs against the yen and the mark as offshore investors bailed out of low yielding currencies.
In New Zealand, dealers said trade had been hectic, with the Aussie's rise squeezing a lot of shorts in the Kiwi and people buying the break.
"It put a lot of pressure on people who were really looking for the Kiwi to break down further," said one dealer.
BT's Pye said there was a feeling in the market that Reserve Bank may have to review its easing stance earlier than it had originally anticipated.
"The general sentiment is changing somewhat. I think we've completed the shorter term downtrend and I think the market will be looking to buy dips back towards the 6870 level now," she said.
Dealers said the Kiwi had not been influenced by the U.S. dollar this session.
The Kiwi was seen trading a 0.6885-25 range overnight.
